model_family: Parent Gaussian-copula random-intercept population with a moment-matched beta-binomial PFS aggregate on the 1/15 lattice; other parametric marginals and outcome-independent correlated attendance retained

evidence_use.operator: per-visit arithmetic mean, sample SD, nonmissing count
evidence_use.population: 75 adults with overweight or obesity; 12-week internet behavioral weight-management program, then 9 months without additional intervention; measurements at months 0,3,6,9,12.
evidence_use.measurement: Clinic weight in kg; PFS total average of 15 1-5 items; No-Go errors integer; delay-discounting AUC separately for $100 and $1000 conditions.
evidence_use.provenance: source_packet_A; supplied target-derived marginals, reconstruction regime A0
evidence_use.reason: Use all 25 visit-specific means and sample SDs as population marginal parameter inputs and all denominators as exact count constraints, scaled by n/75. These same-population reconstruction inputs are not held-out validation. They do not identify any joint distribution.

evidence_use.population: 75 adults with overweight or obesity; 12-week internet behavioral weight-management program, then 9 months without additional intervention; measurements at months 0,3,6,9,12.
evidence_use.measurement: Clinic weight in kg; PFS total average of 15 1-5 items; No-Go errors integer; delay-discounting AUC separately for $100 and $1000 conditions.
evidence_use.reason: Use five scheduled visits, numeric units, bounded scores, integer No-Go errors and baseline enrollment weight cap. Revise PFS to values 1+K/15, K=0,...,60, corresponding to the declared average of 15 integer 1-5 items. Complete integer item scoring is assumed; item-level responses and any missing-item/prorating rules are unavailable. Age, BMI, height, pregnancy and contraindication eligibility cannot be regenerated from the outcome-only schema.

components.name: parametric_marginals
components.source_to_target_assumptions: A0 same-population reconstruction. Weight remains lognormal with baseline parameters solving truncated-lognormal moments for weight <=180 kg; subsequent weight has no upper cap. AUC outcomes remain beta on [0,1]; errors remain negative binomial conditioned on <=512. PFS now follows 1+K/15 for K~BetaBinomial(60,a,b). Its a,b solve the supplied mean and variance analytically; this describes only the aggregate distribution and makes no item-level claim. Distribution shapes, endpoint mass, and applicability of complete integer item scoring remain assumptions. Finite cohort sample moments fluctuate rather than being forced to match inputs.

components.name: longitudinal_gaussian_copula
components.source_to_target_assumptions: Stable person factors provide repeated-measure continuity. Latent variance from person factors is 0.90 for weight and 0.60 for every behavioral endpoint; remaining variance is independent visit noise. The two discounting endpoints each split their 0.60 person variance into 0.30 shared discounting-domain and 0.30 endpoint-specific person variance. Thus their latent cross-endpoint correlation is 0.30. These fixed values are qualitative modeling choices and are not estimated or selected against reserved results. Pearson correlations after marginal transformations need not equal latent values.

components.name: cross_domain_completion
components.source_to_target_assumptions: Independent factors for weight, food responsiveness, inhibition and the discounting domain complete the unspecified joint law parsimoniously. This is an explicit unvalidated independence assumption, not evidence that any association is absent. The model supplies no additional behavior-weight coupling or causal treatment response mechanism.

components.name: exact_count_attendance
components.source_to_target_assumptions: Independent Gaussian attendance factors have variance fractions 0.60 person, 0.30 person-visit and 0.10 endpoint-visit. Ranking them separately for each supplied denominator yields exact observed counts, shared visit nonresponse and persistent but potentially intermittent missingness. Attendance factors are independent of outcome factors, a conditional-count MCAR assumption. Individual masks, missingness causes and informative attrition remain unknown.

components.name: sampling_and_interface
components.source_to_target_assumptions: n counts persons, each with exactly five rows; counts round(n_observed*n/75). New ordinal synthetic keys have no source linkage. A local default_rng(seed) supplies all randomness. Input evidence is read-only; there is no generator filesystem or network access. Marginal sample moments fluctuate across cohorts and are not forcibly matched.

components.name: pfs_measurement_mapping_revision
components.source_to_target_assumptions: The measurement definition supplies a 15-item 1-5 average. The beta-binomial count K represents 60 possible unit increments above the minimum sum, not 60 observed items. With p=(mean-1)/4 and R=(15*sd)^2/[60*p*(1-p)], use precision=(60-R)/(R-1), a=p*precision, b=(1-p)*precision. All five supplied PFS moments are admissible. This corrects continuous support while retaining stochastic sampling and the original copula uniform draws.

scenarios.assumption: The sole target completion preserves the parent within-person persistence, common stable discounting component, independent other domains and outcome-independent correlated attendance. PFS uses a full 15-integer-item aggregate lattice with a beta-binomial shape matching supplied population moments.
scenarios.inclusion_rationale: Select the narrow measurement-mapping revision because it uses an explicit source measurement constraint. No source joint summaries distinguish alternative dependence or attrition parameters, so these parent assumptions are retained without claiming they are correct. Twenty target cohorts are a fixed resource allocation, not a posterior probability.
unresolved_dependencies: All actual within-person correlations, temporal lag effects and random slope heterogeneity
All actual cross-domain correlations and behavior-weight associations
Whether discounting endpoints share person, visit or other components and their strengths
Informative missingness, actual mask overlap, dropout and intermittent return
Distributional shape and endpoint atoms; PFS item response dependence, missing-item rules and rounding conventions
affected_analysis_classes: Baseline pairwise correlations among pfs, gng, dd100 and dd1000
Categorical-visit random-intercept trajectories for all five outcomes

changes_from_parent: Replace only the continuous PFS beta quantile with a moment-matched beta-binomial aggregate quantile on 1/15 increments. Keep the random draw schedule, non-PFS quantiles, latent variance fractions, cross-domain completion, attendance factors, exact scaled counts, keys and interface. Parent source feedback was valid with 25/25, 22/25 and 23/25 marginal envelopes; its five misses are not evidence for a different joint model. No numerical parameters were tuned to eliminate those misses.

source_check_results.interpretation: Source diagnostic envelopes concern reconstruction inputs, not held-out validation. PFS lattice passes on all three scheduled cohorts. Remaining envelope misses are inherited non-PFS sampling deviations; no fitting or seed selection followed them. Controller will attach its own source feedback.

examined_structures.reason: Source-compatible on declared frame checks, but its continuous PFS aggregate ignores the complete 15-item integer-score lattice supplied by the measurement definition. Rejection is based on mapping, not marginal diagnostic ranking or reserved outcomes.

Chosen before new diagnostics to honor the explicit PFS measurement lattice with analytic population moments. No evidence identifies a replacement dependence model. Local checks verify implementation only.

Also request the PFS scoring rule for incomplete items and a per-visit aggregate score frequency table to distinguish discrete families and endpoint atoms.
